title: Operator access sealed-log snapshotter and key-rotation playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We currently capture admin/operator actions and config changes in the admin-audit stream, but we lack a standardized, operator-access-focused procedure to produce tamper-evident snapshots that can be rotated and escrowed across residency boundaries. This ticket defines a playbook + implementation to produce sealed log snapshots (WORM-compatible), rotate sealing keys with HSM/KMS integration, and automate evidence export to escrow buckets with residency metadata. Goals: 1) Produce daily and on-demand sealed snapshots of admin activity that are cryptographically verifiable (hash manifests, Merkle roots, signature chains). 2) Support scheduled and forced sealing key rotation with a clear epoch boundary so proofs remain verifiable across key epochs. 3) Automate push to WORM/immutable storage (object lock or append-only blob) and optional escrow export for legal hold. 4) Provide console and API access for retrieving snapshot manifests and simple proof-of-integrity verification tools for auditors. Constraints: snapshots must respect data residency policies (region tagging, per-customer residency appendices), retention settings (per-customer or organization-level retention rules), and must not expose sensitive audit payloads without appropriate access controls. Deliverables: a sealed-snapshot service, key-rotation operator, escrow exporter, proof verification tooling, console view + download API, and a runbook for key compromise and manual unseal.
acceptance_criteria: Sealed snapshots generated on schedule (daily) and on-demand via API; each snapshot contains a manifest with per-record hashes, snapshot Merkle root, timestamp, and signing key ID.
Snapshots are stored to an immutable/WORM-capable bucket with retention and residency metadata; object lock or append-only configuration applied.
Sealing key rotation implemented: new epoch keys are published, snapshots contain epoch ID; verifier can chain-verify signatures across epochs using stored public attestations.
Automated escrow export runs (daily/weekly) with compressed proof bundles and residency-aware delivery to configured escrow S3/GCS buckets.

Console UI shows latest snapshot status, retention, and provides a one-click download of manifest+proofs; API returns manifest and verification helper; integration tests cover end-to-end verification.
Runbook exists for immediate rotation and revocation if a sealing key is suspected compromised; manual unseal path validated in staging and documented.
Performance: snapshot generation under normal daily volume completes within retention SLO window (<=2 hours for 30M admin events), and snapshotting does not materially increase API latency.
Security sign-off from InfoSec and Compliance recorded in ticket comments.
Automated alerts exist for failed escrow exports or immutable storage misconfiguration.
All artifacts (design doc, PRs, tests, dashboards) linked in ticket.
Documentation updated: runbook, API reference, and Console help text.
Customer-facing migration notes prepared for existing Dedicated/Private customers who will opt into escrow exports.
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Spike (1 week) — prototype minimal sealed manifest format, a signing wrapper using our KMS/HSM SDK, and a small verifier CLI. Validate Merkle-root construction and signature attachments.

Phase 1: Sealed Snapshot Service (2 weeks) — implement snapshot generation pipeline: query admin-audit stream window, compute per-record SHA-256, build Merkle tree, produce manifest JSON, sign manifest with current sealing key, and store payload+manifest to staging immutable bucket.

Phase 2: Key Rotation Operator (1 week) — implement epoch management, publish public attestations, support scheduled rotation and forced rotation via API. Integrate with HSM/KMS for signing; fallback to in-service soft-keys only for local dev environments.

Phase 3: Escrow Exporter & Residency Tagging (1 week) — package snapshot+manifest+proofs into compressed bundle with residency metadata and push to configured escrow destinations; support per-customer routing based on residency rules.
Phase 4: Console & API (1 week) — add snapshot view, download flows, and a verification helper endpoint; add RBAC gating for snapshot downloads (audit_read role).
Phase 5: E2E Tests & Canary Rollout (1 week) — automated verification tests, canary export to internal escrow buckets, monitoring/alerts, SLO validation.
Phase 6: Documentation & Runbook (ongoing during phases) — draft runbook for key compromise, rotation steps, manual unseal, and recovery verification procedures; compliance sign-off.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Sealing key compromise undermines past snapshot trust. Mitigation: design chain-of-attestation so each epoch publishes a public attestation anchored to an external timestamp authority/HSM notarization; provide immediate forced-rotation + re-issuance playbook and customer notification template.

Risk: Escrow export could violate residency/PDPA if misrouted. Mitigation: add strict routing checks and a pre-flight residency policy validation step; escrow destinations must be pre-approved per customer.

Risk: Snapshot generation might overload the database/stream consumer. Mitigation: use read-only snapshotting consumer, paginate windows, backpressure, and incremental snapshotting option for large volumes.
Risk: Immutable storage misconfiguration. Mitigation: automated validation job that asserts object-lock/append-only flags before export; alerts and auto-rollback if misconfigured.
Risk: Large snapshot size causing expensive egress for escrow. Mitigation: use chunked bundles, on-the-wire compression, and configurable retention windows for escrow copies (e.g., weekly vs daily).

runbook: Immediate forced rotation: call /internal/keys/rotate?scope=sealed-snapshots, verify new public attestation published, re-run pending snapshot seals for last 24h.
Revocation path: mark epoch ID as revoked in attestation index and publish signed revocation notice; alert Compliance and affected customers.

Manual unseal (legal hold/recovery): authorized operator retrieves manifest and compressed bundle from escrow, runs verifier CLI with provided attestation public keys; follow step-by-step checklist in Confluence.
Escrow failure remediation: if export fails, move bundles to quarantine bucket and retry with exponential backoff; page on-call SRE after 3 failed attempts.
Rotation rollback: only allowed if new key fails signing verification; follow rollback checklist and notify Compliance + InfoSec within 1 hour.
notes: Prefer SHA-256 for per-record hashing; manifest format must be compact JSON with stable field ordering for deterministic signing.
Consider anchoring Merkle roots weekly to an external timestamping service (e.g., RFC 3161 TSA) for additional non-repudiation assurances.
We must avoid embedding plaintext sensitive fields in escaped snapshots — scrub or redact PII according to retention rules; provide hashed identifiers for linking back to internal query stores.
Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams for on-prem HSM integrations; provide stubbed KMS interface for air-gapped customers that will use customer provided signing appliances.
